records.text: In the second year under King Darius, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came through Haggai the prophet, saying: “Speak now to Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, and to Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, saying:
Haggai the prophet and Zacharias son of Addo prophesied a prophecy over the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel, over them.
Then Zorobabel son of Salathiel and Iesous son of Iosedek arose and began building the house of God in Jerusalem. God’s prophets were with them, helping them.
Then the work of the house of God in Jerusalem ceased, and it remained idle until the second year of the reign of Darius king of the Persians.
‘Thus says the Lord Almighty: These people say, “The time has not arrived to rebuild the house of the Lord.”’”
The word of the Lord came through Haggai the prophet, saying:
“Is it time for you to live in your houses with recessed ceilings, while this house has been laid waste?
When the king was settled in his house and the Lord had given him possession on every side, away from all his surrounding enemies,
the king said to Nathan the prophet, “Look now, I dwell in a cedar house, while the ark of God remains inside the tent.”
Nathan said to the king, “Go and do all that is in your heart, for the Lord is with you.”
And now, thus says the Lord Almighty: Set your hearts upon your ways.
Our way was searched and examined; let us return to the Lord.

You sowed much and brought in little; you ate, but were not satisfied; you drank, but not to intoxication; you clothed yourselves, but were not warmed in them. The one gathering wages gathered them into a bundle with holes.
You shall carry much seed into the field, and gather little; for the locust shall devour it.
You shall plant a vineyard and dress it, but shall neither drink wine nor rejoice in it; for the worm shall devour it.
You shall have olive trees throughout all your borders, but shall not anoint yourself with oil; for your olives shall fall away.
When I afflict you with a scarcity of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven and give back your bread by weight. You shall eat and in no wise be filled.
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Place your hearts upon your ways.
Go up onto the mountain, cut wood and rebuild the house. I will take pleasure in it and be glorified, said the Lord.

They gave silver to the stonecutters and craftsmen, and food, drink and oil to the Sedanin and Sorin, to bring cedar timber from Lebanon to the sea at Joppa, according to the concession of Cyrus king of the Persians to them.

You looked for much, and it came to little; it was brought into the house, and I blew it away. Therefore, thus says the Lord Almighty: Because My house is desolate, while each of you hurries to his own house,
therefore heaven will hold back dew, and the earth will withhold its produce.
but I will show peace: the vine will give its fruit, the earth its produce, and heaven its dew. I will give My people’s remnant all these as an inheritance.

Elijah the prophet, the Tishbite from Thesbon in Gilead, said to Ahab, “As the Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there will be neither dew nor rain these years except through the utterance of my word.”
I will bring a sword upon the land and the mountains, upon grain, wine and oil, and whatever the earth produces, upon people and livestock, and upon all the labors of their hands.”
And I will bring upon you a sword exacting the penalty of the covenant. You shall flee into your cities, and I will send death among you; you shall be handed into enemies’ hands.

Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and all the remnant of the people listened to the voice of the Lord their God and the words of Haggai the prophet, as the Lord their God had sent him to them. The people feared before the Lord.
Haggai, the messenger of the Lord, said to the people, “I am with you, says the Lord.”
Behold, I have commanded you: be strong and courageous. Do not be fainthearted or afraid, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.”

The Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, the spirit of Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of the remnant of all the people. They came in and were carrying out work on the house of the Lord Almighty, their God,
The leaders of the families of Judah and Benjamin, the priests and the Levites arose, of all those whose spirit God had stirred to go up and build the Lord’s house in Jerusalem.
on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year under King Darius.

Who among you saw this house in its former glory? How do you see it now? As though it did not exist before you.

Many of the priests and Levites and leaders of the families—the elders who had seen the first house at its founding, and who saw this house before their eyes—wept with a loud voice; and the multitude cried aloud with joy to raise a song.
The people could not distinguish the sound of the joyful signal from the sound of the people’s weeping, for the people cried out with a loud voice, and the sound was heard far away.

But now be strong, Zerubbabel, says the Lord; be strong, Joshua, son of Jehozadak, the high priest; let all the people of the land be strong, says the Lord, and work, for I am with you, says the Lord Almighty,

Thus says the Lord Almighty: Let your hands be strong, you who hear these words in these days from the prophets’ mouth, from the day when the house of the Lord Almighty was founded, and from when the temple was built.
and My Spirit stands in your midst. Take courage.

triples.relationship: named prophet and rebuilding leaders in the restoration narrative
triples.rationale: Haggai's opening identifies Haggai, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Joshua son of Jehozadak; Ezra names Haggai's prophecy and the rebuilding work of Zorobabel son of Salathiel and Iesous son of Iosedek. The parallel named participants are retained with each text's spellings.

triples.relationship: second year of Darius as the setting for resumed temple work
triples.rationale: Haggai dates his message to Darius's second year; Ezra says the Lord's house remained idle until that second year. The shared regnal year locates the appeal in the narrative's transition from halted work.

triples.relationship: rebuilding delayed before the prophetic appeal
triples.rationale: Haggai reports the people's claim that the rebuilding time has not arrived; Ezra records that work on God's house stood idle until Darius's second year. The narrative supplies the prolonged stoppage to which Haggai's appeal speaks, without equating external force with the people's stated excuse.

triples.relationship: Haggai explicitly identified as the bearer of divine prophecy
triples.rationale: Haggai introduces the Lord's word through the named prophet; Ezra explicitly identifies Haggai as prophesying to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in God's name. This links the named prophetic ministry, rather than merely two anonymous revelation headings.

triples.relationship: contrast between a settled personal house and God's dwelling
triples.rationale: Haggai challenges inhabitants of houses with recessed ceilings while God's house lies waste; David notices that he lives in a cedar house while God's ark remains in a tent. Both contrast domestic comfort with the condition of the divine dwelling, in different historical settings.

triples.relationship: examination of one's way oriented toward the Lord
triples.rationale: Haggai commands the people to set their hearts on their ways; Lamentations describes the way being searched and examined and calls for return to the Lord. Both connect reflection on conduct with a response toward God.

triples.relationship: much sowing but little harvest and frustrated crop enjoyment
triples.rationale: Haggai describes much sowing with little brought in and unsatisfied consumption; Deuteronomy's curse describes much seed with little gathered and denied enjoyment of wine and oil. The connection concerns agricultural futility, without assigning Deuteronomy's named pests to Haggai.

triples.relationship: eating without satisfaction as covenant affliction
triples.rationale: Haggai says the people ate without being satisfied; Leviticus warns of scarcity in which people eat and are not filled. Both treat food that fails to satisfy as an affliction.

triples.rationale: The command to place their hearts upon their ways repeats the earlier command to set their hearts upon their ways. The repetition frames the account of disappointing labor before the concrete rebuilding instruction.

triples.rationale: Haggai directs the people to cut wood and rebuild the house; Ezra describes provision of payment and supplies to bring cedar timber for the rebuilding setting. Both join obtaining wood to the temple work, without identifying the mountain in Haggai with a specific place.

triples.rationale: Haggai attributes the reduced yield to His desolate house while people hurry to their own houses; the earlier challenge contrasts their finished ceilings with His wasted house. The repeated contrast makes the reason for the shortfall explicit.

triples.rationale: Haggai announces heaven holding back dew; Elijah announces that no dew or rain will come apart from his prophetic word before the living Lord. Both make withheld dew an announced divine judgment, without equating the episodes.

triples.rationale: The native Haggai passage says the Lord brings a sword upon land, produce, people and labor; Leviticus warns that God brings a sword exacting covenant penalty. The correspondence preserves sword language rather than replacing Haggai's word with drought.
